Metadata.title: VayuNetra: satellite methane screening for Indian landfills
Metadata.description: VayuNetra finds, verifies and measures methane plumes from Indian landfills in free Sentinel-2 imagery, then turns them into action dossiers for MoHUA, CPCB/SPCBs and municipal corporations.

Hero.eyebrow: Satellite AI for Indian landfill methane
Hero.title: Methane is invisible. VayuNetra makes it visible.

Problem.title: Landfill methane is large, fast-acting and mostly unmeasured
Problem.warming: Methane traps about {value} times more heat than CO₂ over 20 years.

How.title: From a free satellite pass to an action dossier

pass.title: Sentinel-2 pass
pass.text: Free Sentinel-2 imagery arrives about every {days} days. Every new pass over a site is cut into a chip around the landfill.

mbmp.title: MBMP retrieval
mbmp.text: The multi-band multi-pass method compares the two shortwave-infrared bands with earlier clean passes of the same place.

ai.title: AI segmentation
ai.text: A U-Net with a {encoder} encoder, pretrained on Sentinel-2 ({pretraining}) and trained on {plumes} real plumes plus simulated ones, outlines the plume and scores the scene.

gate.title: Physics gate
gate.text: Methane darkens band 12 strongly, band 11 weakly and visible light not at all, and a plume lies along the wind. Fires, moisture and fresh waste fail these tests.

rate.title: kg/h with uncertainty
rate.text: The plume's integrated mass and the ERA5-Land wind give an emission rate with a 68% range. In calm wind no rate is reported.

dossier.title: Action dossier
dossier.text: Each site gets a dossier with the evidence, the rate and the next step for MoHUA, CPCB/SPCBs and the municipal corporation.

Proof.title: Global benchmark on held-out test sites
Proof.intro: VayuNetra against the classic MBMP method, scored on sites the model never saw in training.

auc.title: ROC AUC
auc.meaning: 0.5 is a coin toss: the score cannot tell plumes from clean scenes. The classic method scores {mbmp}, close to that. VayuNetra scores {vayunetra}.

recall.title: Recall by emission rate (t/h)
recall.meaning: Above 3 t/h VayuNetra finds 3 to 6 times more plumes than the classic method. Below 1 t/h it finds fewer: {low} against {lowMbmp}.

iou.title: Plume outline (pixel IoU)
iou.meaning: How well the drawn outline overlaps the true plume: {vayunetra} against {mbmp}, about four times closer.

accuracy.title: Emission rate within ±50%
accuracy.meaning: For {share} of {plumes} real plumes the estimated rate is within ±50% of the published MARS rate. The median ratio is {ratio}, so estimates are not biased high or low.

Proof.operating: At the operating threshold: precision {pV} vs {pM}, recall {rV} vs {rM}, false-alarm rate {fV} vs {fM}.

Honest.title: A free screener, then a confirmation
Honest.tier1Text: Sentinel-2, every new pass, every site. Finds candidates and rules out most surface changes.
Honest.tier2Text: Hyperspectral satellite, OGI drone or ground survey on the flagged cell.
Honest.boundsMeaning: A steady emitter at or above this rate would have produced more flags than we saw.

limits.perPass: Over dense Indian landfills a single pass catches about {share} of plumes of {tph} t/h or more.
limits.small: Below 1 t/h the model finds {recall} of plumes.
limits.finetune: Fine-tuning on Indian backgrounds did not improve held-out detection (AUC ≈ {auc}). The limit is the Sentinel-2 signal against dense urban backgrounds, which is why VayuNetra has two tiers.
limits.truth: In a known-truth test on an Indian background, the estimated rate was {ratio}× the injected rate at {tph} t/h.
limits.deonar: The Deonar T1 event stays unconfirmed until the hyperspectral check.
limits.screening: Every rate on this page is screening-grade.

Initiative.title: Why we built VayuNetra
Initiative.why: Landfill gas can be captured and burned for power, but only where someone has found it. Sentinel-2 is free and passes over every Indian city about every {days} days. We built VayuNetra to turn those passes into site-by-site evidence a municipal corporation or pollution control board can act on.
Initiative.teamText: Team lead: Jiyad Hussain, Amity University, Noida. Built for the Net Zero AI Architecture hackathon.
Initiative.openText: The code is MIT-licensed on GitHub: the worker, the database schema and this website.

Verify.title: Integrity ledger
Verify.intro: Every flag, confirmation result, mitigation commitment, metered reading and monthly scorecard is written into an append-only hash chain, and the chain is time-stamped on Bitcoin through OpenTimestamps. Anyone can check that no record was changed after it was written.

check.title: Check the chain yourself
check.intro: Your browser downloads every entry, recomputes each SHA-256 hash and follows every link. Nothing on this page is taken on trust.
check.ok: All {n} entries check out, and {anchors, plural, =0 {no heads are stamped yet} one {# stamped head matches} other {# stamped heads match}}. Chain head:

broken.payload: Entry #{id}: its text does not match its hash.
broken.entry: Entry #{id}: its entry hash does not check out.
broken.link: Entry #{id}: it does not link to the entry before it.
broken.order: Entry #{id}: an entry is missing before it.
broken.anchor: The stamped head at entry #{id} does not match the chain.

anchors.title: Bitcoin anchors
anchors.intro: Each time the chain grows, its head is sent to two free OpenTimestamps calendars, which commit it to a Bitcoin block within hours. We then check each proof against that block's Merkle root.
anchors.none: No heads stamped yet; the first goes out on the next scheduled run.
anchors.pending: waiting for a block (usually a few hours)

how.title: Verify a proof without us
how.one: Download a head's .txt file and its .ots proof from the table above.
how.two: The .txt file holds the entry number and hash it stamps; the checker above shows the same hash for that entry.
how.three: Drop both files on <link>opentimestamps.org</link> (or run ots verify) to see the Bitcoin block that proves they existed at that time.

Verify.scope: The ledger holds no personal data: no names, emails, notes or report text. A timestamp proves a record existed and has not changed since; it does not turn a screening-grade figure into a verified one.

Sensors.title: Ground sensor network
Sensors.intro: Low-cost methane sensor nodes around each flagged landfill report every 10 minutes. A small model reads the pressure trend, the wind forecast and recent readings, and warns when a rise is likely in the next {h} hours. Falling air pressure pushes landfill gas out, so the warning can come before the level rises.
Sensors.simulatedNote: No sensors are installed yet. The nodes marked Simulated report from a physics-based simulator driven by real weather at each site, so the network, the warnings and the dashboard can be tested before hardware arrives. Simulated data never enters the integrity ledger and never emails anyone.

Sensors.warnText: A rise is likely within 3 hours ({p}).
Sensors.lelText: A reading reached {ppm} ppm, 10% of methane's lower explosive limit. Keep people and flames away and check on the ground.

model.title: The model
model.summary: A {weights}-weight neural network that forecasts a rise {h} hours ahead. On held-out simulated data (Jul–Sep 2025): ROC AUC {auc}; at the alert setting it warned before {warned} of rises, a median {lead} minutes ahead, against {baseWarned} and {lead} minutes for a rate-of-change alarm; about {fw} false warnings per node per week.
model.honest: Trained and tested on simulated readings, so these numbers describe the simulator, not real air. Retrain on real readings before relying on it; a warning is screening-grade and calls for a check on the ground.
